text:
ana: quick sync — i want to propose a hypothesis-driven roadmap for console observability. aim: cut alert fatigue and surface cost regressions earlier. low risk, experiment-first.

kai: sounds good. do you mean we run small experiments (canaries) per feature and measure a couple of key signals? :+1:

ana: exactly. proposed signals: 1) 95th p50 latency for route X, 2) token cost per request for top 10 customers, 3) spike rate of error-class `response_parse`.

sam: can we add model-quality drift for generation endpoints? e.g., BLEU/ROUGE-ish or prompt-based checks per rollout.

ana: yes — model-quality drift as a secondary signal for v1. primary for v1 should be latency, cost, and error counts.

zephyr: customer asks: our top enterprise wants per-route token-cost breakdown + historical change alerts. they flagged unpredictable billing as blocker.

maria: noted. per-route cost metric is doable if we emit token_count + route tags at request time. storage cost is small. we need to decide retention window for alerting.

lucy: from design: we should show a simple time-series + delta and a single-click `investigate` that pre-fills traces and recent requests. mockups incoming.

ana: here's the lightweight experiment plan i sketched:
- week 0: instrument token_count + route tag for 10% traffic (canary) by shard
- week 1: surface time-series on console for canary customers only, add daily delta alert (20% change)
- week 2: attach `investigate` link -> traces + sample requests
- week 3: evaluate by signals and CS feedback, decide rollout

kai: implementation notes:
```
// emit example (pseudo)
metric("tokens", token_count, {route: route_name, model: model_id, customer: org_id})
```
we'll need a small router hook and metric forwarder. estimate 3d for hook + 2d for dashboard.

sam: tracing hook: attach trace_id to request metadata so console can open trace view filtered by trace_id. we can reuse existing trace ingestion. ~1d.

maria: for alerts, recommend we use both absolute threshold + made-up anomaly score. anomaly model needs 2 weeks of history, so fallback to % delta for v1.

ana: launch criteria (v1 canary):
- token_count emitted for >=10% traffic and visible in console for canary orgs
- daily delta alert created and fired correctly during test window
- `investigate` opens trace + samples within 5s
- CS sign-off from @zephyr after 1 week of canary

kai: tradeoffs: per-route downstream cost pipeline for full customer base is heavier (storage + query). for now limit retention to 7d for v1, then iterate.

maria: logging/PII check — ensure we never log prompt contents in metrics or trace samples. redact before storing. security review required before prod rollout.

lucy: design note: show cost delta as both absolute $ and %age. small sparkline + top contributing routes. mock attached later.

zephyr: i'll coordinate with the customers on the canary cohort. will ask them to opt-in.

ana: owner split: kai = infra + hook, sam = tracing integration, lucy = UI, maria = infra/security + rollout gating, zephyr = CS feedback. i'll own the roadmap and acceptance.

kai: quick question — what about quantization/encoding changes that affect token_count? we need a stable definition of token_count. suggest we use tokenizer library X v1.2 across services.

ana: good point. standardize on tokenizer v1.2 and add `tokenizer_version` tag in metrics. v1 acceptance requires consistent token counts for test prompts.

obs-bot: deploybot: canary deploy scheduled for 2026-06-08T09:00Z for service-apirouter (target 10% traffic).

ana: next steps: kai + sam start instrumenting this week, lucy to produce 2 mocks by Thu, maria schedule security review, zephyr to confirm two canary customers.

kai: ack. will create RFC PR with implementation plan and rough timeline.

sam: will add a small eval that checks model-quality drift on top 20 prompts weekly. low-cost.

ana: thanks all. quick follow-up: if we hit big cost spikes in canary, we pause rollout and trigger fallback policy. document fallback later.

lucy: tl;dr: hypothesis-driven experiments, minimal v1 scope (7d retention), clear launch criteria, customer canary. :rocket:

ana: assigning tasks in the doc. i'll capture minutes and link here.
